His win was the reward for perseverance throughout the summer and he fully deserved his initial Club prize for walking. L. E Storey, one of the bright hopes of the future, walked well to gain second place and showed that he is equally at home on road or track
Martin, once again showed up well until the straight was reached and then faded away, finally finishing fourth. The 2 mile Handicap Walk was won in good style by L.

Our other man, L. Storey, finished ninth and so we scored 29 points.
In the 2 miles Club Walk Handicap, L. Storey maintained his recent good form and won easily, Heather was second and Charlie Speechley third.

Len Storey had been in third position practically throughout the race, and he, too, can take pride in his time. If he shows the same ability and determination that featured his racing on this day, in the "Junior" Championship, we shall have another first-rate man in our team.
LEN STOREY, in finishing 12th, gave us his best performance yet on the road. Throughout he walked with scrupulous fairness and intense determination.

Staines (Leicester) was leading the field, Charlie Churcher being our first man in 6th position, Percy Wright and Jack Rutland together 10th and 11th, and Charlie Redgrave 26th. Len Storey was leading the "B" team in 27th position, Charlie Speechley 29th (he was "gonged" a little while after this) and C.

When these men are joined by others, such as Don Brown, Fred Bentley, Bill Treacher, Len Storey, Jack Rutland, Reg. Elson, Eddie Heather and others, we may be sure our "Junior and "Senior" teams will command respect.
Heather and L. Storey, all experienced "Junior" racing men, have not been able to train regularly this year, but we hope to have their assistance next year.
Len Storey is another old 'un to visit us recently. How about bringing your togs next time, Len?
